title: Bloom is out: 14 PSX space horror infected characters, $7.99
bodyHtml:
Bloom is out. 14 low poly PS1-style infected crew of a deep space station, the enemies for a science fiction survival horror game, rigged and animated for Godot 4, Unity and Unreal: $7.99, with a free sampler on this page.

The cast: a rigger and an ore miner in orange jumpsuits, an EVA technician in a cracked pressure undersuit, a lab technician, a security officer, the galley cook, the captain, the medic, a shuttle pilot, the comms officer, a reactor technician, the company executive, the hydroponics technician where it started and the first host. Every one an adult, each a different body and painted outfit, about 1,500 triangles and one 256 px texture per skin, three palettes each. One contagion on all of them: grey skin, milky eyes and a crusted pale fungal growth through torn clothing, dark dried stains and no open gore. No badges, logos or text anywhere.

Rigged and animated: 45 clips on one standard humanoid skeleton, in GLB, FBX, OBJ and Blender formats, plus our PSX shader for Godot 4. Bloom is part 1 of our space horror set and the other half of Deep Station: that pack is the living crew, this one is what hunts them, on the same skeleton.

Tested before release: the pack gate and its break test, a blank Godot 4.7 import of every GLB with the shader compiled under three renderers, and every FBX and OBJ reopened in Blender. The files on this page were compared with our release folder before upload: 145 of 145 identical, and 15 of 15 for the sampler.

Try it free: the sampler on this page is the first host, with all three skins and every clip. The PSX Character Library holds our PSX packs on one page and takes in every new one; Bloom joins it in the Library's next update.

Count so far: 29 paid PSX packs; 9 of our PSX pages have sold, 32 purchases in all.

Made with AI tools: the bodies were generated by scripts an AI system wrote, and every texture is an AI image model's painting projected onto the mesh. The skeleton and clips are the CC0 Quaternius Universal Animation Library.
